non_bypass_rule: No strategy, quant model, agent, UX component or execution adapter may skip Risk or Pre-Trade Firewall.

verdict_contract.rule: A new or larger position cannot exceed the lesser of strategy request and Risk-authorized limits.

risk_engine.policy_change_rule: Risk policy/ceiling changes require governed configuration/policy change; Risk runtime cannot self-increase ceilings.

rules: intent_id is globally stable for the logical trade intent
intent is provider-neutral
provider-specific symbol/order fields are prohibited here
quantity may be reduced to Risk-authorized maximum but never increased
expired signal/risk verdict cannot create a valid intent

checks: signal still valid and not expired
RiskVerdict exists, is current and policy version is valid
instrument is mapped and provider capability exists
no unresolved execution state conflicts with this intent/scope
positions/open orders snapshot is sufficiently fresh
post-intent exposure remains inside Risk limits
liquidity/spread/slippage hard bounds pass when policy requires
credential capability is valid and least privilege
fail_closed_conditions: unknown outstanding order that can alter exposure
pretrade_firewall.rule: Firewall may reject/halt but cannot relax Risk limits or invent missing state.

approved_trade_intent.rule: Only an unexpired ApprovedTradeIntent may enter OMS. It remains provider-neutral.

critical_state_rules: UNKNOWN is not a retryable-success or final-reject state.
UNKNOWN blocks a new execution-capable route for the same exposure until reconciled.
PARTIALLY_FILLED updates remaining exposure; any additional routing requires fresh Risk/Firewall evaluation where material.
Local timeout does not prove provider rejection.
Provider/exchange execution facts override local assumptions, while local intent/audit history is preserved.

identities.intent_id: Stable identity of the logical approved trade intent.
identities.route_attempt_id: Unique identity for one provider routing attempt.
identities.provider_client_order_id: Provider-facing idempotency/client order identity mapped to route attempt.

rules: Retry to the same provider reuses safe idempotency semantics where provider supports them.
A network timeout never creates a new logical intent.
Only one unresolved execution-capable route attempt per intent/exposure is permitted by default.
A second provider route is forbidden while first-route execution status is UNKNOWN.
Reroute is allowed only after deterministic proof the earlier route cannot execute, or after reconciliation/cancel/fill resolution and fresh Risk/Firewall approval.
Blind cross-broker replay is forbidden.
Provider/exchange is authoritative for actual external order/fill/position facts.
Local system is authoritative for original intent, Risk/Firewall decisions and audit history.
Mismatch creates ReconciliationEvidence and blocks unsafe new orders for affected scope.
Reconciliation never silently rewrites audit history.
After material reconciliation, Risk/Firewall state is refreshed before new exposure.

safe_sequence: obtain fresh Risk/Firewall approval for future intents
execution_failover.rule: Provider failover cannot assume an unacknowledged order was not executed.

rules: Halting is easier than re-enabling.
No runtime actor may increase risk ceilings as part of recovery.
Re-enable requires health/reconciliation checks and policy-defined authorization.
EMERGENCY_FLATTEN is distinct from GLOBAL_HALT because closing positions itself creates market/execution risk.
All kill-switch transitions and authorities are audited.

behavior.DEGRADED: Affected scopes may restrict new exposure; Risk/Firewall applies stricter policy.
behavior.SAFE_MODE: No new risk-increasing exposure; only explicitly permitted defensive/reduce actions.
behavior.HALTED: No new execution except explicit recovery/defensive policy.
behavior.RECOVERY: Reconciliation and health validation before return to NORMAL.

rules: ApprovedTradeIntent includes environment and account scope.
Credential handles are environment/account/provider bound.
SHADOW can observe and simulate decisions but cannot emit live provider commands.
DEMO routes only to simulation/practice execution.
CANARY/LIVE remain disabled until later roadmap gates.
Cross-environment credential/state reuse is forbidden unless explicitly designed as read-only reference.
Execution domains receive credential handles/references, not raw secrets in ordinary data contracts.
Trading credentials must be least privilege.
Withdrawal/transfer permission is disabled/not requested where provider supports separable permissions.
Credential validity and capability are checked before execution.
Credential compromise triggers security halt/revocation path.

audit_evidence.rule: A material execution outcome must be traceable end-to-end by correlation_id without storing raw secrets.

P24: canary/live capital activation and owner gates
